source.title: Novelty facilitates the persistence of aversive memory extinction by dopamine regulation in the hippocampus and ventral tegmental area.

confidence_rationale: Causal rodent behavioral-tagging study: exposure to a NOVEL context around encoding converts an otherwise-decaying weak memory into a persistent one, and this is causally dopamine/VTA-dependent (VTA NMDA stimulation mimics novelty; VTA muscimol inhibition abolishes both the persistence and the hippocampal dopamine rise). Provides the CELLULAR/causal substrate for a novelty-gated write and confirms the dopaminergic conjunction at synaptic level. Held to 0.6 for the operationalisation verdict: it demonstrates that NOVELTY (an external contextual event) gates persistence, but does not arbitrate novelty-vs-PE nor address the goal/value-anchor specificity -- it is mechanistic grounding, not adjudication. | 2026-06-24 tag-join: DEV-NEED-006 (the developmental WRITE-gate sub-need of MECH-189 -- high-salience benefit contact written to a durable super-ordinal goal anchor) added to claim_ids_tested. This paper evidences that WRITE gate as faithfully as it does MECH-189; the addition joins existing prior art to the DEV-NEED-006 experiment tag (v3_exq_588e) and clears a false novel_discovery quadrant flag that arose only because the experiment was tagged to the gate id while the literature was tagged to the parent claim.
failure_signatures: Persistence of a weak memory required a dopaminergic novelty/salience event around encoding (behavioral tagging and capture); a write gate lacking any such modulatory-event term would let load-bearing-but-weak contacts decay -- the INV-075 self-extinguishing-signal failure mode.
VTA inhibition abolished both the novelty-induced persistence and the hippocampal dopamine increase, confirming the write gate is dopaminergically mediated and not a passive similarity computation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In rats, exploring a novel context for 5 min around a weak extinction-learning episode produced persistent extinction over 21 days and raised hippocampal dopamine. Intra-CA1 dopamine infusion or VTA glutamatergic (NMDA) stimulation reproduced the effect; VTA GABAergic (muscimol) inhibition blocked the persistence and lowered hippocampal dopamine -- demonstrating behavioral tagging and capture gated by the dopaminergic novelty signal.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the cellular-level justification for MECH-189 even HAVING a separate complexity/novelty gate: a high-salience contact that is not accompanied by a novelty/surprise event may fail to persist (decay), whereas one that co-occurs with novelty is captured into durable storage. It confirms gate (b) is a real, dopamine-mediated modulator of write persistence, and that the salience and novelty terms converge on the same dopaminergic machinery (consistent with Lisman-Grace).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The 'novelty' here is an experimentally-injected separate contextual event (explore a novel box), operationalised as environmental unfamiliarity, not as 1 - similarity to a goal-anchor store nor as a graded PE. It is aversive extinction memory in rodents, not a cross-episode super-ordinal goal write. So it grounds the EXISTENCE and dopaminergic nature of the gate but does not by itself favour the self-contained novelty proxy over an external PE signal.
mapping.source_context: Male Wistar rats; inhibitory-avoidance extinction; behavioral tagging via novel-context exposure; intra-CA1 and intra-VTA pharmacology.

confidence_components.notes: Solid causal rodent pharmacology. Mapping fidelity moderate: it grounds the gate's existence and dopaminergic mediation but the 'novelty' construct is an injected contextual event, not the REE proxy or a PE. Transfer risk elevated: rodent aversive-extinction memory -> abstract super-ordinal goal write.
